# Depressive disorders

*Categories: Clinical knowledge > Emergency medicine > Psychiatric disorders > Depressive disorders*

[Original Article Link](/library/Kv0UaR)

---

## Summary

Depressive disorders are a group of conditions manifesting with <u>symptoms of depression</u> that impair an individual's ability to function. They include <u>major depressive disorder</u> (<u>MDD</u>), <u>premenstrual dysphoric disorder</u> (<u>PMDD</u>), <u>disruptive mood dysregulation disorder</u> (<u>DMDD</u>), <u>persistent depressive disorder</u> (<u>dysthymia</u>), <u>depressive disorder due to another medical condition</u>, and <u>substance/medication-induced depressive disorder</u>. Depressive disorders are typically identified during routine screening or examination. The diagnosis is clinical based on <u>DSM-5</u> criteria after <u>exclusion of organic causes of depression</u> and <u>differential diagnoses of depressive symptoms</u>. Treatment varies based on the specific diagnosis but typically includes <u>psychotherapy</u>, and/or medication.




<u>Major depressive disorder</u> and <u>premenstrual dysphoric disorder</u> are covered in separate articles.

---

## Overview

### <u>Epidemiology</u>




Varies depending on the underlying disorder, e.g.:




* Lifetime <u>prevalence</u> for <u>MDD</u> of ∼ 20% [[2]](/library/psYLDq)

* Annual <u>prevalence</u> for <u>PMDD</u> of 1–8% [[3]](/library/muWV7M0)[[4]](/library/lEdvD70)

* <u>Substance/medication-induced depressive disorder</u> is rare.  [[3]](/library/muWV7M0)





### Clinical features [[3]](/library/muWV7M0)




* <u>Symptoms of depression</u> (e.g., low mood, <u>anhedonia</u>)

* Somatic features may be present depending on the condition (e.g., <u>somatic symptoms of PMDD</u>)

* Symptoms may not be reported, but can be identified through <u>screening for depression</u>.





### Diagnosis [[3]](/library/muWV7M0)




* <u>Clinical diagnosis</u> based on the relevant <u>DSM-5</u> criteria.

* Exclude <u>differential diagnoses of depressive disorders</u>.

* Depending on symptoms, consider <u>workup for organic causes of depression</u>.





### Differential diagnoses of depressive disorders [[3]](/library/muWV7M0)




* <u>Bipolar affective disorder</u>

* <u>Personality disorder</u>

* <u>Adjustment disorder</u>

* <u>Bereavement and grief</u>

* <u>Burnout syndrome</u>





### Management [[3]](/library/muWV7M0)




* Treatment is specific to the underlying disorder but usually includes <u>psychotherapy</u> and/or <u>antidepressants</u>.

* Screen for and treat concurrent disorders (e.g., <u>substance use disorder</u>, <u>anxiety</u>).

* Refer patients with severe or refractory symptoms, <u>suicidal ideation</u>, and/or <u>psychotic features</u> to <u>psychiatry</u>.

* See also:

* “<u>Treatment for depression</u>”

* “<u>Management of PMDD</u>”

* “<u>Treatment of DMDD</u>”





### Types of depressive disorders [[3]](/library/muWV7M0)




| <br><u>Overview of depressive disorders</u>  [[3]](/library/muWV7M0)<br> |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Condition | Timing of symptoms | Selected clinical features |
| <u>Major depressive disorder</u> | <br>* Present for at least 2 weeks<br><br> | <br>* ≥ 5 symptoms from the <u>diagnostic criteria for MDD</u><br><br> |
| <u>Persistent depressive disorder</u> (<u>dysthymia</u>) | <br>* Present for ≥ 2 years<br><br> | <br><br>* <u>Depressed mood</u><br><br>* ≥ 2 <u>clinical features of persistent depressive disorder</u><br><br><br> |
| <u>Major depressive disorder with seasonal pattern</u> | <br><br>* Typically occurs in the fall or winter<br><br>* Present for ≥ 2 years<br><br><br> | <br><br>* Symptoms are the same as those in <u>MDD</u>.<br><br>* Onset and remission at specific times of the year<br><br><br> |
| <u>Premenstrual dysphoric disorder</u> (<u>PMDD</u>) | <br><br>* Start ≤ 1 week before and resolve ≤ 1 week after onset of <u>menses</u><br><br>* Present during most <u>menstrual cycles</u><br><br><br> | <br><br>* ≥ 1 <u>premenstrual affective symptoms</u><br><br>* ≥ 1 <u>premenstrual somatic symptoms</u><br><br><br> |
| <u>Mood disorder</u> due to another medical condition | <br>* Variable<br><br> | <br>* Symptoms attributable to another condition, e.g.:<br><br>* Endocrinopathies<br><br>* <u>CNS</u> disorders<br><br>* <u>Malignancy</u><br><br> |
| <u>Substance/medication-induced depressive disorder</u> | <br>* Variable<br><br> | <br>* Symptoms attributable to use of or withdrawal from a substance e.g.:<br><br>* <u>Recreational drugs</u><br><br>* <u>Systemic glucocorticoids</u><br><br>* <u>Hormonal contraceptives</u><br><br> |
| <u>Disruptive mood dysregulation disorder</u> (<u>DMDD</u>) | <br>* Present for ≥ 12 months with onset before 10 years of age<br><br> | <br><br>* Severe temper with outbursts ≥ 3 times per week<br><br>* Irritability or anger in between outbursts<br><br>* Diagnosis must be made between 6–18 years of age.<br><br>* Increased risk for <u>MDD</u> and/or <u>anxiety disorders</u> in adulthood<br><br><br> |

## Persistent depressive disorder

<u>Persistent depressive disorder</u> (<u>dysthymia</u>) is a chronic depression characterized by a consistently low mood and additional depressive symptoms lasting for ≥ 2 years (≥ 1 year in <u>adolescents</u> and children). [[3]](/library/muWV7M0)




### Diagnosis [[3]](/library/muWV7M0)[[5]](/library/4GY3zq)




* Diagnosis is confirmed using the <u>DSM-5 diagnostic criteria for persistent depressive disorder</u>.

* Often occurs concurrently with other psychiatric conditions (e.g., <u>MDD</u>, <u>personality disorders</u>).

* Assess severity to help determine management:

* Mild: Symptoms are manageable.

* Moderate: Symptoms are mild to severe.

* Severe: Symptoms are severe, unmanageable, and significantly exceed the requirement for diagnosis.





> [!TIP]
> Depressive disorders are frequently identified during <u>screening for depression</u>. [[3]](/library/muWV7M0)




#### DSM-5 diagnostic criteria for persistent depressive disorder [[3]](/library/muWV7M0)




Diagnosis is confirmed in individuals who meet all of the following criteria.




* <u>Depressed mood</u>

* In adults: most of the day for the majority of days for ≥ 2 years

* In children and <u>adolescents</u>: irritable or <u>depressed mood</u> for ≥ 1 year

* ≥ 2 of the following clinical features of persistent depressive disorder

* Overeating or poor appetite

* <u>Sleep</u> disturbance (<u>insomnia</u> or <u>hypersomnia</u>)

* Fatigue, loss of energy

* Poor self-esteem

* Diminished concentration and decision-making ability

* Hopelessness

* Symptoms clinically significant <u>distress</u> or impaired functioning in important areas of life (e.g., work, school)

* Periods of remission last ≤ 2 consecutive months.

* Features of differential diagnoses are not present.

* No history of <u>manic</u> or <u>hypomanic episodes</u>

* Symptoms are not due to:

* Persistent <u>schizoaffective disorder</u> or another <u>psychotic disorder</u>

* Effects of substances or organic disease





> [!TIP]
> <u>Thoughts of suicide</u>, loss of interest, and <u>psychomotor agitation</u> or retardation may manifest in PDD but are not part of the diagnostic criteria. [[3]](/library/muWV7M0)




> [!NOTE]
> HE'S 2 SAD: Hopelessness, Energy loss or fatigue, Self-esteem is low, 2 years minimum of <u>depressed mood</u>, Sleep is increased or decreased (<u>insomnia</u> or <u>hypersomnia</u>), Appetite is increased or decreased, Decision-making and/or concentration is impaired.




### Treatment [[5]](/library/4GY3zq)




Treatment of <u>persistent depressive disorder</u> is the same as <u>treatment for depression</u>.

---

## Depressive disorder due to another medical condition

* <u>Depressed mood</u> and/or <u>anhedonia</u> attributable to a general medical condition

* Conditions associated with depressive disorder include the following:

* <u>Hypothyroidism</u>

* <u>Primary adrenal insufficiency</u>

* <u>Stroke</u> (especially <u>anterior cerebral artery</u> <u>stroke</u>)

* <u>Parkinson disease</u>

* <u>CNS</u> <u>neoplasms</u>

* Other <u>neoplasms</u> (e.g., <u>pancreatic cancer</u>)

* <u>Dementia</u>

* Parathyroid disorders

* See also “<u>Depression in patients with cancer</u>” and “<u>Depression post myocardial infarction</u>.”

---

## Substance/medication-induced depressive disorder

* <u>Depressed mood</u> and/or <u>anhedonia</u> attributable to the use of, or withdrawal from, substances or medications

* Substances or medications associated with depressive disorder include the following:

* <u>Marijuana</u>, γ-hydroxybutyric acid (<u>GHB</u>), flunitrazepam, <u>ketamine</u>

* <u>Alcohol</u>

* <u>Corticosteroids</u>

* <u>Oral contraceptive pill</u>

---

## Disruptive mood dysregulation disorder

<u>Disruptive mood dysregulation disorder</u> (<u>DMDD</u>) is a depressive disorder characterized by extreme irritability and severe recurrent outbursts of anger (verbal or behavioral) that do not meet criteria for <u>bipolar disorder</u>. [[3]](/library/muWV7M0)




### <u>Epidemiology</u> [[3]](/library/muWV7M0)




* <u>♂</u> > <u>♀</u>

* <u>ODD</u> and other depressive disorders are common comorbidities. [[7]](/library/zUXrfx)





### Etiology




Causes currently being investigated include psychological trauma and/or abuse, <u>malnutrition</u>, <u>vitamin deficiencies</u>, and neurological problems (e.g., <u>migraine</u>).




### DSM-5 diagnostic criteria for DMDD [[3]](/library/muWV7M0)




* Severe, recurrent outbursts of anger (verbal or behavioral) toward people or property, disproportionate in intensity or duration to the situation that:

* Are not appropriate to developmental stage (e.g., <u>temper tantrums</u>)

* Occur on average ≥ 3 times per week

* Persistently irritable mood between outbursts (observed by parents, peers, teachers)

* Symptoms are present:

* Before the age of 10 years

* For ≥ 12 months, within which time there has been no consecutive period of ≥ 3 months without symptoms

* In ≥ 2 settings (i.e., home, school, or with peers); severe symptoms occur in ≥ 1 setting

* The symptoms are not better explained by <u>differential diagnoses of DMDD</u>, e.g.:

* Criteria for a <u>manic</u> or <u>hypomanic episode</u> have never been met for longer than 1 day

* Symptoms do not occur exclusively during a <u>major depressive episode</u>

* <u>Substance use disorder</u> and other medical and neurological conditions have been ruled out.

* The diagnosis is made between 6 and 18 years of age.





### Differential diagnoses of DMDD [[3]](/library/muWV7M0)




* <u>Autism spectrum disorder</u>

* <u>Posttraumatic stress disorder</u>

* <u>Separation anxiety disorder</u>

* <u>Persistent depressive disorder</u>

* <u>Bipolar disorder</u>

* <u>Oppositional defiant disorder</u>

* <u>Intermittent explosive disorder</u>

* <u>ADHD</u>





> [!WARNING]
> Some differential diagnoses, e.g., <u>ADHD</u>, can also be comorbid with <u>DMDD</u>, however, individuals with a diagnosis of <u>ODD</u>, <u>intermittent explosive disorder</u>, or <u>bipolar disorder</u> cannot also be diagnosed with <u>DMDD</u>. [[3]](/library/muWV7M0)[[8]](/library/f6dk4I0)




### Treatment of DMDD [[9]](/library/TDd6dH0)




As <u>DMDD</u> is a relatively new psychiatric diagnosis, there is limited evidence for its treatment.




* Treat comorbidities (e.g., <u>ADHD</u>, <u>mood disorders</u>).

* Refer for psychosocial interventions, e.g.:

* Family support and parenting classes

* <u>Cognitive behavioral therapy</u> or <u>dialectical behavior therapy</u>

* Refer patients with severe <u>DMDD</u> to a <u>psychiatrist</u> for consideration of pharmacotherapy (e.g., <u>antidepressants</u>). [[9]](/library/TDd6dH0)[[10]](/library/G6dBmI0)[[11]](/library/F6dg5I0)





### Prognosis [[3]](/library/muWV7M0)




Individuals with <u>DMDD</u> are at increased risk of <u>major depressive disorder</u> and <u>anxiety disorders</u> in adulthood.
